newsitem.title: USA: NASD kicks off media campaign to educate investors.
newsitem.headline: NASD kicks off media campaign to educate investors.

text.p: National Association of Securities Dealers said Wednesday it will launch an unprecedented broadcast media campaign soon to educate the public on how to be smarter investors.
The initiative is the "first coast-to-coast public service announcement television and radio campaign ever undertaken" by a securities market regulator, NASD said in a press statement.

The announcements, which are expected to run soon about 15,000 times on 300 stations in 200 cities and other media markets, include three "spots," said NASD, which settled Securities and Exchange Commission charges last year that it was too lax in enforcing securities rules.
One advertisement tells investors how to do background checks on the securities brokers they have hired or may want to hire using NASD's Central Registration Depository.

CRD is a computer system that allows investors to track the disciplinary histories and backgrounds of brokers and securities firms. The toll-free number for the CRD information service is 800-289-9999.

Two other spots tell viewers and listeners how to use NASD's WEB site at www.investor.nasds.com, which trains investors about how to take control of their personal finances, work with brokers and how to calculate the value of their investments, NASD said.

NASD vice president Michael Jones, head of the association's new Office of Individual Investor Services, said a recent NASD survey found that only 14 percent of Americans can tell a growth stock from an income stock.
Only 12 know the difference between a "load" and "no-load" fund, he said.
"There is a real need for quality investor education that investors can make use of in the privacy of their own homes," Jones said.
"While 63 percent of Americans know the difference between a halfback and a quarterback, only 14 percent can tell the difference between a growth stock and an income stock," Jones said.
